Thanks for surfacing this, Amit. Short answer: commits can be supported either way, but the economics differ. Quick summary and two concrete options for BuyCo:  

Marketplace vs Direct — what to expect
- AWS Marketplace path: AWS charges a marketplace fee (varies by program, typically 5–20% depending on private offer terms); that fee is effectively additive on top of Redwood’s list price unless we absorb or rebate it.
- Direct Redwood invoice path: discounts are applied directly to list per-token rates and reflected on Redwood invoices; no marketplace fee applied.

Two options for BuyCo (numbers are illustrative; I’ll attach worksheet):
Option A — Marketplace Private Offer (preferred by BuyCo procurement)
- Redwood posts a private offer through AWS Marketplace at list prices; AWS fee applies at the marketplace level (e.g., 12% in our example).
- Redwood can offer a "Marketplace Net Match" credit: we give a monthly rebate back to BuyCo for the difference so net-per-token equals our direct committed price. This requires a reconciliation/credit process and a legal note in the PO.

Option B — Direct Commitment with Redwood
- BuyCo signs a direct commitment (monthly token commit), Redwood issues invoices directly, and the commit tier discounts apply immediately.
- If BuyCo still wants the marketplace experience for procurement, we can provide an invoice-backed attestation for BuyCo finance to justify a marketplace-led PO, but the net accounting will be direct Redwood billing.

Concrete example (150M tokens/month target):
- Redwood direct committed price (tiered average): $0.0003/token => $45,000/month
- Marketplace list price plus AWS 12% fee: $0.0003 * 1.12 = $0.000336/token => $50,400/month
- To match net, Redwood would provide a monthly rebate of $5,400 under the Marketplace Net Match credit (Option A) for an initial bridging period.

Attachments: I’ve uploaded a simple worksheet demonstrating the math (redwood-pricing-grid-v2.xlsx and aws-marketplace-fees-breakdown.pdf).

Caveats: credits complicate bookkeeping and require finance approval. Also our legal team needs to review language for private offers and credits.

If BuyCo prefers, we can propose a 6-month "marketplace match" credit to start and then transition to direct billing for long-term reporting simplicity.

—Priyom

Hi Amit / BuyCo team — looping in Redwood legal and finance to make sure we land this cleanly. I’ve reviewed Priyom’s example and support a short-term accommodation to match net-marketplace economics for strategic customers. Proposed path: 

1) Initial 6-month Marketplace Net Match: Redwood will provide a monthly credit equal to the marketplace fee difference to achieve the same net-per-token as a direct commitment, subject to:
   - Signed Private Offer (AWS marketplace) AND a short MPA addendum that describes the rebate mechanics (payment timing, reconciliation cadence).
   - Finance approval to process monthly credits (these will appear as credit memos on Redwood invoices).
2) After 6 months, we re-evaluate and either: convert to direct billing (recommended) or renew the marketplace match with a formal pricing schedule.
3) We cannot combine the same commitment across both Marketplace and Direct billing simultaneously for the same token volume — commitments must be scoped to one billing path.

Next steps for BuyCo:
- Procurement to issue a Private Offer request in AWS marketplace (we’ll respond with the Private Offer price).
- Sign the MPA addendum we’ll provide (legal@redwood.com will send draft).
- Provide PO referencing the Private Offer so we can create the credit schedule.

I’ll have Naomi coordinate finance mechanics and send a template credit memo. Priyom, please prepare the formal pricing worksheet for 150M tokens and include monthly credit column.

Karthik Iyer
VP, Commercials
